correctness.rationale: Under orthogonal diagonalization, \(Q_Z(A)=v^{\mathsf T}Wv/24-\sum_{i<j}w_{ij}a_{ij}^2/12\). For nonzero Z, W is nonzero trace-zero, hence at least one positive direction; any negative \(w_{ij}\) adds another positive. For \(w_{ij}\)>=0, Perron–Frobenius and trace zero show that W has either one or two positive eigenvalues, with second positive iff det W>0. The direct polynomial identity \(\det W=-4(e_1e_3-4e_4)\) proves the exact equivalence including zeros. All normalization factors and rational counterexample values were checked by symbolic coefficients of det(tA+rZ+uI), with a standalone verifier. Reverse CS follows from one-positive inertia and the PSD principal minors. Boundary Z=0 explicitly excluded.

originality.rationale: The dated 2026 primary paper proves the base-case signed mixed-discriminant AF inequality under a sufficient spectral-balance condition, not an if-and-only-if four-dimensional inertia criterion. Its Prop. 4.5 makes the trace-zero hyperplane negative, whereas the new classification allows a positive index one while that hyperplane can fail to be negative. Direct expansion and Perron–Frobenius give a non-implied determinant boundary; the signed spectral-positive counterexample has an explicit strictly positive-definite AF failure. Generalized AF for dually Lorentzian differential operators covers positive-definite reference forms, not this fixed indefinite signed spectral threshold. Materially relevant primary sources were read; incomplete historical coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: An older unindexed spectral theorem for quadratic mixed discriminants could imply the determinant criterion; semantic search absence is not a novelty certificate.

value.rationale: The 2026 source explicitly extends Alexandrov–Fenchel beyond convex reference forms with only a sufficient balance cone. A complete necessary-and-sufficient four-dimensional spectral boundary is a natural missing problem, not an arbitrary parameter choice; signed configurations outside the balance cone show genuinely broader nontrivial valid inequalities. The rational PD counterexample precisely distinguishes spectral positivity from hyperbolicity, while zero-boundary cases are included. It identifies a sharp structural test with immediate proof-theoretic and geometric significance; general n or multiple references are not claimed.
